notes: Australia's independent national regulator for online safety, established under the Online Safety Act 2021 (Cth). Registers and enforces mandatory Industry Codes and Industry Standards under Part 9 of the Act.

data.description: Australian federal statute establishing the eSafety Commissioner, basic online safety expectations (BOSE), cyber-abuse and image-based abuse takedown schemes, the Social Media Minimum Age framework (under-16 restriction enacted via the 2024 Amendment Act), and enforceable Part 9 Industry Codes and Standards.
data.notes: Status: In force (commenced January 23, 2022; amended by the Online Safety Amendment (Social Media Minimum Age) Act 2024; verified as of 2026-11-03).

data.official_name: Registered Online Safety Industry Codes (Phase 2 — Class 1C and Class 2 Material)
alternate_names: Relevant Electronic Services and Designated Internet Services Codes (Phase 2 — Class 1C and Class 2 Material)
data.description: Legally enforceable Phase 2 industry codes registered by the Australian eSafety Commissioner under Part 9 of the Online Safety Act 2021 addressing Class 1C and Class 2 material (high-impact pornography, R18+/X18+ content, and self-harm/suicide themes), requiring age assurance, risk assessments, safety-by-design controls, and crisis guardrails across 8 industry sectors explicitly including conversational AI chatbots and AI companions.
data.notes: Status: In force (the Internet Search Engine Services Phase 2 code commenced December 27, 2025, and the remaining 7 Phase 2 codes — Social Media Services, App Distribution Services, Hosting Services, Internet Carriage Services, Equipment, Relevant Electronic Services, and Designated Internet Services including conversational AI companions — commenced March 9, 2026, with specific equipment sub-measures having phased compliance dates in June 2026; verified as of 2026-11-03). Note: Phase 1 Industry Codes covered Class 1A and Class 1B material (CSAM, pro-terror, and extreme crime/violence); Phase 2 covers Class 1C and Class 2 material. Classified under type 'regulation' because registration under Part 9 of the Online Safety Act 2021 makes compliance legally binding and enforceable via eSafety directions, enforceable undertakings, injunctions, and civil penalties up to 50,000 penalty units (~AU$49.5 million).
